drivers.driver: The normalized earnings yield of equities significantly exceeds the long-bond yield, presenting a superior risk-adjusted return profile [D02][D04].
Broad market panic, evidenced by the VIX at 67.61 and systemic credit stress, has pushed prices below intrinsic value for many high-quality businesses [D03][D04].
Long-term ownership of productive businesses remains the superior path to wealth compared to the nominal claims of government instruments [D01].
Economic fear is extreme, creating the conditions to be 'greedy when others are fearful' while avoiding distressed or leveraged entities that risk permanent loss of capital [D05].

final.memo:
We are currently witnessing a period of acute fear where market participants are liquidating indiscriminately, driven by the financial crisis and credit impairment [D03]. When we look at the arithmetic, the normalized earnings yield of equities, adjusted for the temporary compression in reported earnings, stands at a substantial premium to the yield on 10-year Treasury bonds [D02][D04]. This spread signals that stocks are objectively cheap for those who focus on sustainable distributable cash rather than tomorrow's quote [D01].

Our process remains unchanged. We are not predicting an economic recovery or a market bottom; we are simply observing that the prices of many wonderful businesses are now detached from their intrinsic value [D01][D03]. While we remain disciplined—avoiding companies with unsustainable leverage or those requiring a favorable credit environment to survive—we are finding sufficient opportunities to deploy capital into businesses that possess durable competitive advantages and pricing power [D01][D05]. We will continue to act as owners, ignoring the daily volatility in favor of the long-term compounding of our capital [D01].
